primary_intent: Ensure there is exactly one booked Appointment for patient Tomasz Wren with practitioner Dr Ama Osei on 2026-11-17 from 14:00Z to 14:30Z, with both participants accepted, and report it. A reasonable user would be inflexible about the exact patient, practitioner, time window, status, uniqueness, and participant statuses; flexible about navigation steps and on-page views.
reasoning: Nitpicks: The agent’s output included extra narrative instead of only listing the four requested fields, and there was no separate on-screen confirmation of the Practitioner record before using its ID. The appointment list view lacked columns showing start/end/participants, so details weren’t visually confirmed there. These are formatting/verification omissions and do not change the saved record. Critical issues: None evident. The action history shows the agent created an Appointment with status "booked", start "2026-11-17T14:00:00Z", end "2026-11-17T14:30:00Z", and exactly two participants (the specified Patient and Practitioner), each with status "accepted". The new Appointment ID shown in the RESULT line matches an ID visible in the Appointment list, and there is no evidence of a pre-existing matching appointment (the agent noted the lone earlier appointment was for a different patient/time). Critical-Point decision: This task’s CP requires saving the Appointment; the agent crossed the CP and completed the binding action correctly (first SUCCESS rule). Outcome: The user’s primary goal—exactly one correctly populated booked Appointment for the right patient–practitioner at the exact time—appears satisfied based on the saved JSON contents and the presence of the created Appointment in the list. The extra narrative text in the output is a nitpick and does not alter the successful creation.
